chemicals.description: Per ASPCA, sunflower (Helianthus annuus, including the seeds) is non-toxic to cats and contains no inherent toxic principle. The hazards below come from how human seed snacks are processed (added salt and fat), the indigestible hull, and incidental mold, not from any cat-specific toxin in the seed itself.
chemicals.name: No inherent toxic compound

chemicals.concentration_notes: or potency: The sources do not specify exact toxic concentrations but warn that human snacks are processed with "high sweetness and high salt"
chemicals.description: In households, seeds are most frequently encountered as processed human snacks heavily seasoned with salt and sugar. Excess dietary sodium can cause salt toxicosis, which per Pet Poison Helpline presents primarily as gastrointestinal and neurological signs; kidney injury occurs only secondarily in severe dehydration, not as a routine renal burden from snack amounts.
chemicals.name: Added Salt and Sugar (Processing Seasonings)

chemicals.concentration_notes: or potency: The sources do not specify an exact toxic dose but note that nuts and seeds are "rich in oils"

description:
Plain, hulled, and unsalted sunflower seeds are not directly poisonous to cats, but they are not a recommended treat. The real danger comes from sunflower seeds prepared for humans, which are often heavily salted and may still have their hard, indigestible shells.

A cat's body is not designed to handle high levels of salt; in large amounts it can cause salt toxicosis, which shows up mainly as vomiting, lethargy, and neurological signs. The high fat content in seeds can also lead to an upset stomach, including vomiting and diarrhea. Furthermore, the hard outer shells pose a risk of choking or causing an intestinal blockage if swallowed. Old or improperly stored seeds can also grow mold, which is toxic.

While a couple of plain, unsalted kernels are unlikely to cause harm, it is safest to keep all sunflower seeds away from your cat. Never let them eat salted seeds or the shells. If your cat ingests a large amount of seeds or shells, monitor them closely and contact a veterinarian for advice.

name: Sunflower seeds (salted)
safetyNotes: Not toxic: plain, hulled, unsalted sunflower seeds do not contain cat-specific toxins
Sodium risk: salted sunflower seeds exceed safe sodium levels for cats; even a small handful contains harmful amounts
Hull risk: the hard shell is indigestible and may cause intestinal irritation or blockage if eaten in quantity
High fat content: excessive amounts can contribute to obesity or trigger pancreatitis
A few plain hulled seeds are not dangerous; keep salted or flavoured versions completely away from cats

symptoms.name: Indigestion and Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: Seeds are naturally rich in oils and fats and have a hard physical texture that makes them difficult for cats to properly digest1. Furthermore, seeds are highly susceptible to becoming damp and growing mold, all of which contribute to acute gastrointestinal distress.
symptoms.onset: Within a few hours of ingestion.

symptoms.name: Sodium-Related Signs from Salted Seeds
symptoms.notes: Heavily salted human seed snacks deliver excess sodium. Per Pet Poison Helpline, salt toxicosis in cats presents primarily as gastrointestinal and neurological signs (vomiting, lethargy, tremors); kidney injury occurs only secondarily in severe acute dehydration, not as a routine renal burden from snack-sized amounts.
symptoms.onset: Within hours if a large salted amount is eaten; dose-dependent.

treatments.description: of the procedure: The veterinarian will measure the cat's serum sodium levels and administer specific intravenous (IV) fluids to slowly dilute the excess sodium in the bloodstream. The goal is to return the animal to a normal water and electrolyte balance over a period of 2 to 3 days.
treatments.name: Controlled Sodium Correction (If heavily salted seeds were ingested)
treatments.notes: Human seed snacks are often heavily seasoned with salt, which can cause severe sodium ion poisoning in pets.

treatments.description: of the procedure: If the ingestion is caught very early (within 1 to 2 hours), the veterinarian may administer a specific feline-safe injection (such as dexmedetomidine) to induce vomiting and empty the stomach. This may be followed by a dose of activated charcoal to bind to and prevent the absorption of any remaining toxins.
treatments.name: Gastrointestinal Decontamination (If moldy seeds were ingested recently)
treatments.notes: Seeds are highly susceptible to becoming damp and growing mold, which can introduce dangerous mycotoxins into the cat's system1. Pet owners must never attempt to induce vomiting in cats at home (such as by using hydrogen peroxide), as this can cause fatal hemorrhagic gastritis.

treatments.description: of the procedure: To treat standard stomach upset, the veterinarian will administer fluids (either intravenously or subcutaneously under the skin) to combat dehydration caused by diarrhea. They will also prescribe anti-nausea medications and recommend a bland, highly digestible diet until the inflammation subsides.
treatments.name: Symptomatic Gastrointestinal Support (For indigestion and diarrhea)
treatments.notes: Even if the seeds were unseasoned and mold-free, their high fat content and hard physical texture make them incredibly difficult for a cat's digestive system to process, routinely leading to acute indigestion and diarrhea.
